neighbours.label: a verb of failure or decay under negation ('will not fail', 'do not expire', 'cannot be exhausted', 'does not spoil')
fire: The gift cards never expire, so there is no rush to spend them.
Stored in a cool cellar, the potatoes will not rot until spring.
Engineers promised that the new pumps would not fail during a flood.
These membership points do not expire as long as your account is open.
Honey sealed in a jar does not spoil, even after many years.
The well is so deep that it cannot be drained even in a dry summer.
Good stainless steel will not rust if you dry it after washing.
The supply of wind on that coast simply cannot be exhausted.
quiet: The gift cards are printed with a gold border and a short message.
Stored in a warm shed, the potatoes rotted within a few weeks.
Engineers warned that the old pumps would fail during a flood.
These membership points do not appear until the end of the month.
Milk left in the sun turns sour after only a few hours.
The well is so deep that we needed a very long rope for the bucket.
Cheap steel will rust quickly if you leave it wet after washing.
The wind on that coast blows hardest in the late winter months.

predictions: 7/8 fire; the same verbs without negation, and negated neutral verbs, stay quiet
notes: Probe: 'do not expire' 1.033, 'cannot be exhausted' 0.880, 'will not fail' 0.500, 'does not spoil' 0.290; 'will not charge' 0.010, 'will fail quickly' 0.031, 'spoiled quickly' 0.032.
